chapters.name: Biomolecules
keyPoints: Biochemical Fractions: Acid-soluble pool contains micromolecules ($<1000\text{ Da}$); acid-insoluble fraction contains macromolecules (proteins, nucleic acids, polysaccharides) and membrane lipids.
Protein Hierarchy: Polymers of 20 amino acids linked by peptide bonds; tertiary structure determines 3D active site conformation; quaternary structure involves multi-subunit complexes (Hemoglobin).
Carbohydrate Polymers: Cellulose (unbranched $\beta$-glucose), Starch ($\text{I}_2$-trapping helical $\alpha$-glucose), Glycogen (branched storage), Chitin (N-acetylglucosamine).
Enzymatic Catalysis: Enzymes lower activation energy of transition state; affected by temperature, $\text{pH}$, and competitive inhibitors (malonate competing with succinate).
Cofactor Classes: Essential non-protein constituents classified as firmly bound prosthetic groups (haem), transient coenzymes (NAD/niacin), or metal ions ($\text{Zn}^{2+}$).

chapters.name: Photosynthesis in Higher Plants
keyPoints: Photophosphorylation Pathways: Non-cyclic photophosphorylation (PS II and PS I) produces ATP, $\text{NADPH}$, and $\text{O}_2$ via photolysis; cyclic photophosphorylation (PS I only) produces ATP alone.
Chemiosmotic ATP Synthesis: Protons accumulate in the thylakoid lumen; diffusion through $\text{CF}_0\text{-}\text{CF}_1$ ATP synthase drives photophosphorylation.
Calvin Cycle ($\text{C}_3$): Primary $\text{CO}_2$ fixation by RuBisCO onto RuBP produces 3-PGA; fixing $6\text{CO}_2$ consumes $18\text{ ATP}$ and $12\text{ NADPH}$.
$\text{C}_4$ Adaptations: Kranz anatomy and initial fixation by PEP carboxylase in mesophyll avoids photorespiration, increasing photosynthetic efficiency in high temperatures.

chapters.name: Respiration in Plants

formulas.name: Respiratory Quotient (RQ)
formulas.latex: RQ = \frac{\text{Volume of } CO_2 \text{ evolved}}{\text{Volume of } O_2 \text{ consumed}}

keyPoints: Glycolysis (EMP Pathway): Cytoplasmic conversion of 1 glucose to 2 pyruvate yielding a net gain of $2\text{ ATP} + 2\text{ NADH}$ without oxygen.
Link Reaction & Krebs Cycle: Mitochondrial matrix oxidation converts pyruvate to Acetyl-CoA, yielding $6\text{ NADH}, 2\text{ FADH}_2, 2\text{ GTP}$, and $4\text{ CO}_2$ per glucose.

Electron Transport System: Complexes I–IV transfer electrons to terminal $\text{O}_2$ while pumping protons; Complex V ($\text{F}_0\text{-}\text{F}_1$) generates ATP ($1\text{ NADH} = 3\text{ ATP}, 1\text{ FADH}_2 = 2\text{ ATP}$).
Respiratory Quotient: Measures $\text{CO}_2$ evolved per $\text{O}_2$ consumed (Carbohydrates $= 1.0$, Fats $= 0.7$, Proteins $= 0.9$).

chapters.name: The Living World
keyPoints: Defining Criteria of Life: Cellular organisation, metabolism, and consciousness define living organisms without exception; growth and reproduction are non-defining.
Binomial Nomenclature: System by Linnaeus using Latinised binomials (Genus species Author); genus capitalized, species lowercase, italicized in print or separately underlined when written.
Taxonomic Hierarchy Order: Obligate sequence from specific to general is Species $\to$ Genus $\to$ Family $\to$ Order $\to$ Class $\to$ Phylum/Division $\to$ Kingdom.
Taxonomic Invariance: Number of shared similarities decreases as one ascends the taxonomic hierarchy from species to kingdom.

chapters.name: Biological Classification
keyPoints: Whittaker's Five Kingdoms: Classifies Monera (prokaryotic), Protista (unicellular eukaryotic), Fungi (heterotrophic eukaryotic with chitin walls), Plantae (autotrophic cellulosic), and Animalia (holozoic, no cell wall).
Bacterial Diversity & Archaebacteria: Monera exhibits highest metabolic diversity; Archaebacteria survive extremes due to unique branched-chain lipid cell wall architecture.
Protistan Adaptations: Diatoms form indestructible diatomaceous earth; Dinoflagellates produce red tides (Gonyaulax); Euglenoids possess flexible protein pellicle.

Fungal Taxonomy: Classified into Phycomycetes (coenocytic), Ascomycetes (endogenous ascospores in asci), Basidiomycetes (exogenous basidiospores on basidia), and Deuteromycetes (imperfect, no sexual stage).
Acellular Pathogens: Viruses consist of protein capsid surrounding DNA or RNA (never both); Viroids are free low-MW RNA lacking capsid; Prions are infectious folded proteins.

chapters.name: Plant Kingdom
keyPoints: Algal Pigmentation & Storage: Chlorophyceae (Chl $a, b$, starch in pyrenoids), Phaeophyceae (Chl $a, c$, fucoxanthin, laminarin/mannitol, algin), Rhodophyceae (Chl $a, d$, r-phycoerythrin, floridean starch).
Bryophyte Generation Alternation: Dominant gametophyte produces gametes in multicellular antheridia and flask-shaped archegonia; sporophyte remains attached and nutritionally dependent.
Pteridophyte Evolution: First terrestrial plants with vascular tissues (xylem/phloem); sporophyte is dominant; heterospory (Selaginella) serves as a precursor to seed habit.
Gymnosperm Naked Seeds: Ovules remain exposed on megasporophylls before and after fertilization; gametophytes have no independent free-living existence.

chapters.name: Animal Kingdom
keyPoints: Fundamental Body Architecture: Invertebrates and chordates are classified by symmetry (radial vs. bilateral), coelom (acoelomate, pseudocoelomate, eucoelomate), and embryonic germ layers.

Unique Phylum Markers: Porifera (choanocytes, canal system), Cnidaria (cnidoblasts, metagenesis), Ctenophora (comb plates, bioluminescence), Platyhelminthes (flame cells, flat acoelomates), Aschelminthes (pseudocoelomate, muscular pharynx).

Coelomate Adaptations: Annelida (metamerism, nephridia), Arthropoda (jointed appendages, chitinous exoskeleton, Malpighian tubules), Mollusca (radula, mantle, visceral hump), Echinodermata (water vascular system, adult radial).
Chordate Hallmarks: Characterized by notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, pharyngeal gill slits, and post-anal tail; divided into Urochordata, Cephalochordata, and Vertebrata.

Vertebrate Classes: Cyclostomata (jawless), Chondrichthyes (cartilaginous, placoid scales, claspers), Osteichthyes (bony, operculum, swim bladder), Amphibia (cloaca, moist skin), Reptilia (epidermal scutes, cleidoic eggs), Aves (feathers, pneumatic bones), Mammalia (mammary glands, hair).

chapters.name: Morphology of Flowering Plants
keyPoints: Root & Leaf Configurations: Taproots develop from radicle, adventitious from other parts; phyllotaxy is alternate, opposite, or whorled; venation is reticulate (dicots) or parallel (monocots).
Floral Symmetry & Ovary Insertion: Flowers are actinomorphic (radial) or zygomorphic (bilateral); ovary is superior (hypogynous), half-inferior (perigynous), or inferior (epigynous).
Aestivation Modes: Arrangement of sepals/petals in bud includes valvate, twisted, imbricate, and vexillary (papilionaceous).
Placentation Types: Ovule arrangement in ovary is marginal (pea), axile (lemon, tomato), parietal (mustard with replum), free central (Dianthus), or basal (sunflower).
Solanaceae Profile: Potato family characterized by $\oplus \ \text{\textdied} \ K_{(5)} \ \overbrace{C_{(5)} \ A_5} \ \underline{G}_{(2)}$ with persistent calyx and swollen axile placenta.

chapters.name: Anatomy of Flowering Plants
keyPoints: Tissue Systems: Epidermal (cells, cuticle, stomatal apparatus, trichomes), Ground (parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma), and Vascular (xylem and phloem).
Vascular Bundle Configurations: Radial (roots) vs. Conjoint (stems/leaves); Open with cambium (dicot stem) vs. Closed without cambium (monocot stem).
Root Anatomy: Dicot root has diarch-tetrarch xylem and small pith; monocot root has polyarch ($>6$) xylem and large pith; endodermis bears suberized Casparian strips.
Stem & Leaf Differentiation: Dicot stem has vascular bundles in a ring; monocot stem has scattered bundles in ground tissue; monocot leaves possess bulliform cells for rolling.

chapters.name: Structural Organisation in Animals
keyPoints: Poikilothermic Amphibian Adaptation: Rana tigrina exhibits camouflage, hibernation, and aestivation; skin is moist, vascularized, and performs cutaneous respiration.
Digestive & Excretory Anatomy: Short alimentary canal, bilobed tongue; ureotelic excretion via kidneys; male ureters act as urinogenital ducts opening into cloaca.
Circulatory Features: 3-chambered heart (2 atria, 1 ventricle) with sinus venosus and conus arteriosus; closed double circulation with hepatic and renal portal systems.
Reproductive Pathways: Male testes connect via 10–12 vasa efferentia to Bidder's canal; females lay 2500–3000 eggs; development is indirect via aquatic tadpole metamorphosis.

chapters.name: Cell: The Unit of Life
keyPoints: Cell Theory Axiom: All living organisms are composed of cells arising from pre-existing cells via division (Omnis cellula-e cellula by Virchow).
Prokaryotic Structure: Lacks membrane-bound organelles; possesses peptidoglycan wall, mesosome infoldings, naked circular DNA with plasmids, and 70S ribosomes.
Fluid Mosaic Membrane: Singer-Nicolson model describes a phospholipid bilayer with mobile integral/peripheral proteins and cholesterol, exhibiting selective permeability.
Endomembrane System: Coordinated network comprising Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER for protein, SER for lipid), Golgi (glycosylation/packaging), Lysosomes (acid hydrolases), and Vacuoles (tonoplast).
Semiautonomous Organelles: Mitochondria (cristae, ATP generation) and Chloroplasts (thylakoids/grana, stroma) possess circular DNA, 70S ribosomes, and divide by fission.

chapters.name: Cell Cycle and Cell Division
keyPoints: Interphase Sequence: Comprises $G_1$ (growth/organelle duplication), S (DNA replication doubles content $2\text{C} \to 4\text{C}$, chromosome number $2n$ unchanged), and $G_2$ (tubulin/protein synthesis).
Mitotic Stages: Prophase (condensation), Metaphase (equatorial alignment at metaphase plate via kinetochores), Anaphase (centromere splitting, chromatid migration), Telophase (envelope reformation).

Prophase I Sub-stages: Leptotene (visibility) $\to$ Zygotene (synaptonemal complex, synapsis) $\to$ Pachytene (crossing over via recombinase) $\to$ Diplotene (chiasmata formation) $\to$ Diakinesis (terminalisation).

Meiotic Outcome & Significance: Homologous separation in Anaphase I reduces chromosome number by half ($2n \to n$); sister chromatid separation in Anaphase II yields 4 genetically variable haploid gametes.

chapters.name: Plant Growth and Development
keyPoints: Growth Kinetics: Arithmetic growth exhibits linear elongation ($L_t = L_0 + rt$); geometric growth follows a sigmoid curve ($W_1 = W_0 e^{rt}$).
Growth Promoters: Auxins mediate apical dominance and rooting; Gibberellins induce bolting and seed germination; Cytokinins promote cytokinesis and delay senescence.
Growth Inhibitors: Ethylene promotes fruit ripening and abscission; Abscisic Acid (ABA) acts as a stress hormone by inducing stomatal closure and bud dormancy.
Cellular Plasticity: Differentiation produces specialized cells; dedifferentiation restores meristematic ability; redifferentiation forms mature secondary tissues.

chapters.name: Breathing and Exchange of Gases
keyPoints: Lung Capacities: Vital Capacity ($\text{VC} = \text{TV} + \text{IRV} + \text{ERV} \approx 4500\text{ mL}$); Functional Residual Capacity ($\text{FRC} = \text{ERV} + \text{RV}$).
Alveolar Gas Exchange: Governed by partial pressure gradients ($p\text{O}_2 = 104\text{ mm Hg}$ in alveoli vs. $40\text{ mm Hg}$ in deoxygenated blood; $p\text{CO}_2 = 40$ vs. $45\text{ mm Hg}$).
Oxygen Transport: $97\%$ bound to hemoglobin as oxyhemoglobin; sigmoid dissociation curve shifts right with high $p\text{CO}_2$, high $\text{H}^+$, and elevated temperature.
Carbon Dioxide Transport: $70\%$ transported as bicarbonate ions ($\text{HCO}_3^-$) via carbonic anhydrase, $23\%$ as carbaminohaemoglobin, $7\%$ in plasma solution.
Respiratory Control: Medullary rhythm center and pontine pneumotaxic center regulate breathing based on $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}^+$ concentrations.

chapters.name: Body Fluids and Circulation
keyPoints: Formed Elements: Erythrocytes (gas transport), Leucocytes (neutrophils/monocytes phagocytic, lymphocytes immune, basophils inflammatory), Platelets (thromboplastin release).
Coagulation Cascade: Thrombokinase converts prothrombin to thrombin, which polymerizes soluble fibrinogen into an insoluble fibrin meshwork in the presence of $\text{Ca}^{2+}$.
Cardiac Mechanics: SAN initiates rhythm ($72\text{ beats/min}$); cardiac output equals stroke volume $\times$ heart rate ($\approx 5\text{ L/min}$).
ECG Waves: P-wave (atrial depolarization), QRS complex (ventricular depolarization), T-wave (ventricular repolarization).
Double Circulation: Complete separation of systemic and pulmonary circuits prevents mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.

chapters.name: Excretory Products and their Elimination
keyPoints: Nitrogenous Excretion: Animals are ammonotelic (aquatic, highly toxic), ureotelic (mammals/amphibians, urea), or uricotelic (birds/reptiles, uric acid paste).

Urine Formation Steps: Glomerular ultrafiltration ($\text{GFR} = 125\text{ mL/min}$) $\to$ Tubular reabsorption (PCT reabsorbs $70\text{--}80\%$ water/solutes) $\to$ Tubular secretion ($\text{H}^+, \text{K}^+$ into lumen).
Counter-Current Mechanism: Henle’s loop and vasa recta maintain hyperosmolar medullary gradient ($300 \to 1200\text{ mOsmol/L}$) to concentrate urine.
Endocrine Feedback: RAAS mechanism (Renin $\to$ Angiotensin II $\to$ Aldosterone) and ADH increase water retention; ANF promotes vasodilation and $\text{Na}^+$ excretion.

chapters.name: Locomotion and Movement
keyPoints: Sarcomere Sliding Mechanism: $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ binds Troponin C to expose actin sites; myosin cross-bridges pull actin toward M-line, shortening I-band and H-zone while A-band remains constant.
Muscle Filament Proteins: Thin filament contains F-actin, tropomyosin, and troponin; thick filament consists of meromyosin with globular ATPase heads.
Skeletal Divisions: Human skeleton has 206 bones divided into 80 axial (skull, vertebral column, ribs, sternum) and 126 appendicular (girdles and limbs).
Synovial Joint Varieties: Freely movable joints including ball & socket (shoulder/hip), hinge (elbow/knee), pivot (atlas/axis), and saddle (thumb).

chapters.name: Neural Control and Coordination
keyPoints: Resting Membrane Potential: Maintained at $-70\text{ mV}$ by differential permeability ($\text{K}^+ > \text{Na}^+$) and active $\text{Na}^+/\text{K}^+$ ATPase pump ($3\text{ Na}^+$ out / $2\text{ K}^+$ in).
Action Potential Generation: Threshold stimulus triggers voltage-gated $\text{Na}^+$ influx, causing rapid depolarization to $+30\text{ mV}$, followed by $\text{K}^+$ efflux for repolarization.
Synaptic Transmission: Action potential induces $\text{Ca}^{2+}$-mediated neurotransmitter exocytosis across synaptic cleft to open ligand-gated channels on postsynaptic membrane.
Brain Functional Regions: Cerebrum coordinates sensory/motor associations; Corpus callosum connects hemispheres; Hypothalamus controls homeostasis; Medulla regulates autonomic vitals.

chapters.name: Chemical Coordination and Integration
keyPoints: Pituitary Master Control: Anterior pituitary secretes tropic hormones (GH, TSH, ACTH, LH, FSH); posterior pituitary stores oxytocin and vasopressin (ADH).

Metabolic & Calcium Regulators: Thyroid hormones ($\text{T}_3/\text{T}_4$) govern basal metabolic rate; Parathyroid hormone (PTH, hypercalcemic) opposes Thyrocalcitonin (TCT, hypocalcemic) for $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ homeostasis.
Adrenal & Pancreatic Hormones: Adrenal medulla secretes catecholamines (fight-or-flight); cortex releases Aldosterone and Cortisol; Pancreatic Insulin lowers and Glucagon raises blood glucose.

Mechanisms of Hormone Action: Peptide hormones act via membrane receptors and second messengers ($\text{cAMP}, \text{IP}_3, \text{Ca}^{2+}$); steroid and thyroid hormones bind intracellular receptors to regulate gene expression directly.
